title: GnuPG key folder
whyItMatters: The GnuPG folder holds the private keys that decrypt mail and files and sign commits. With the passphrase they are a full identity; without it, the key names and recipients still show who the person talked to.
source: GnuPG manual, the home directory defaults to ~/.gnupg and holds keyrings and private keys: https://gnupg.org/documentation/manuals/gnupg/GPG-Configuration-Options.html
notes: private-keys-v1.d holds the private keys, pubring.kbx the public keys and trustdb.gpg the trust database. The folder is mode 700 and readable by its owner; GNUPGHOME can move it elsewhere.

cleanup.exportFirst: Export a backup of your public and private keys with the Passwords and Keys app, or with Kleopatra on KDE, and keep the backup off this computer.
steps: Open the key backup you exported and check that it holds the keys you still need.
Close mail, chat and code tools that may be using the keys.
Move the folder named in the plan to the Trash and empty the Trash.
cleanup.risk: Deletes your private keys, so encrypted mail and signed commits stop working and files encrypted to these keys stay unreadable without the backup.
cleanup.source: GnuPG Manual, GPG configuration options and the home directory: https://gnupg.org/documentation/manuals/gnupg/GPG-Configuration-Options.html
